Welcome from the Headteacher
Welcome to Greenmount Primary School.
Arrange a Personal Visit
Experience Greenmount Primary School firsthand. Tailored to your child’s interests and admission stage, we offer visits year-round, from Preschool to Year 6.
Admissions
Please click on the link below for more information on admissions.
The Ethos and the Environment
We aim to provide a stimulating, caring and safe environment for all of our children and their families, for our staff, volunteers and governors. We strive to offer a wide range of opportunities to support and challenge the learning community at Greenmount to perservere, achieve success and develop skills and attributes to live full and rewarding lives.
A Happy Learning Environment
Our mission is to ignite a lifelong passion for learning. By challenging the advanced and uplifting the less assured, we ensure each pupil realizes their unique academic potential. Together, we nurture the future.
We look forward to welcoming you to Greenmount Primary School.
Greenmount Primary School
St Vincent’s Road, Ryde, Isle of Wight, PO33 3PT

pageCache.pageTitle: Absences and Holiday Requests – Greenmount Primary School
pageCache.text:
Absences and Holiday Requests
Absences
If, for any reason, your child is to be absent from school due to illness or an accident, please let the school know by 8:30am on the first day of absence. This can be done by phoning the school (selecting Option 1 from the menu), sending an email to absences@greenmount.iow.sch.uk or messaging the .Absence account in ClassDojo.
Holiday Requests
As parents, you have the legal responsibility to ensure your child’s regular attendance at school. Applications for leave of absence will only be granted in exceptional circumstances and the number of days given determined by the Headteacher.
If you wish to apply for a leave of absence for your child in term time, you will need to complete a Application for Leave of Absence form and return it to the school office no later than 14 days before the requested date. A copy of the form can be collected from the School Office.
Any leave of absence during term time which is not applied for or agreed to by the school will be recorded as unauthorised and will be referred to the Local Authority. This may result in a Truancy Penalty Notice (TPN) being issued or Prosecution under Section 444 Education Act for failure to secure regular attendance at school.

Governors Committees
The Governing Body are responsible for:
Governing Body members take a lead in the monitoring and review of their assigned areas of responsibility and report back to the Board.
The Full Governing Body meets twice a term.
Headteacher’s Performance Management Panel
Pupils’ safety and wellbeing is a fundamental issue for all governors to be aware of so is covered on every agenda of the Full Governing Body meetings.
The Meeting Planner provides details of all Governor meetings scheduled for the current academic year.
Approve expenditure requests as necessary.

pageCache.pageTitle: After School Club – Greenmount Primary School
pageCache.text:
After School Club
The Afterschool Club runs during term time each afternoon between 3pm and 5.45pm and caters only for children who attend Greenmount Primary School.
Children attending the club must be collected from school at the end of each session by a responsible adult. The club offers all children a snack and drink upon arrival and a light tea for those children who are with us after 4pm. A range of activities will be available to all children and these are designed to provide a settled but stimulating end to their school day. There will be opportunities to read, complete homework and access computers if the children wish to do so.
Please click on the video below to see an overview of our provision:
The fee structure is as follows:
Afterschool session (1 hour – or part of)
Afterschool session(2Hr 45 – or part of)(Full session – includes a light tea)
After registration, all spaces must be booked via ParentPay.
All fees must be paid for via ParentPay in advance, or at the time of booking.
If a child misses a session, charges may still apply.
Spaces must be booked via ParentPay by Midday on the day before the required session.
Last minute spaces may be available depending on numbers but your account must be in credit for us to book these. (Please call the office)
Cancellation: You can cancel any booked session up to midday on the day before the session and a credit will be applied to your account. Cancellation after this time may incur a charge. (Please call the office)
The governing body of the school is responsible for the club, and the provision is under constant review. The governors and club staff reserve the right to refuse to take children who are either unhappy being left at the club, or whose behaviour is unacceptable. Concerns will, of course, be discussed with parents/carers before any decision is made.

Breakfast Club
From September 2026, our school is proud to be in partnership with the National School Breakfast Programme, providing healthy breakfasts to our pupils so that they are settled and ready to learn.
The National School Breakfast Programme (NSBP) is funded by the Department for Education and delivered by Family Action to support schools in England to provide children with a healthy breakfast at the start of the school day.
The Breakfast Club runs during term time each morning between 7.30am and the beginning of each school day, and caters only for children who attend Greenmount Primary School. All children attending the club must be brought into school by a responsible adult.
Children attending the club will be offered a balanced healthy, nutritious breakfast and a range of activities will be available to all children which are designed to provide a settled but stimulating start to their day.
After registration, all spaces must be booked via Parent pay.
All fees must be paid for via ParentPay in advance, or at the time of booking.
If a child misses a session, charges may still apply.

The governing body of the school is responsible for the club, and the provision is under constant review. The governors and club staff reserve the right to refuse to take children who are either unhappy being left at the club, or whose behaviour is unacceptable. Concerns will, of course, be discussed with parents/carers before any decision is made.

ClassDojo
What is ClassDojo?
At Greenmount, we use ClassDojo as our main form of communication with parents. The app can be installed on a smartphone or tablet (android or iOS) and allows us to communicate with one another: instantly sharing messages, updates, events, and photos from class. It’s simple, secure, and gives a window into your child’s school day. You can use the app to notify the school of child absences too.
How do I register?
If you are a parent of a child in the school and do not have the app, please contact the school office. You will be sent an email invitation to join.
Help with ClassDojo
If you have any issues with registering or using ClassDojo, please contact the school office (contactus@greenmount.iow.sch.uk) and we will be happy to assist you.

PTA
We are a group of parents and teachers who volunteer to fundraise for Greenmount Primary school. Every parent/guardian who has a child attending Greenmount, or any member of staff, can be a member of the PTA. We hold regular meetings, generally at school, to plan and discuss fundraising ideas and events. All are welcome to attend.
Do you have a skill that you would like to share, such as computer knowledge, book keeping, crafting, design or anything that you think the PTA could benefit from? Would you like to join or know more about our PTA? Please email us at pta@greenmount.iow.sch.uk.
The PTA are always looking for volunteers to help run events, so if you would like to lend a hand in any way, please get in touch. Any help is always appreciated.

PE & Sport
We are determined to provide a stimulating, caring and safe environment for all of our children and their families and for our staff, volunteers and governors. We strive to offer a wide range of opportunities to support and challenge the learning community at Greenmount to persevere, achieve success and develop skills and attributes to live full and rewarding lives. PE, sport and physical activity is an excellent vehicle to achieve this. The Sports Premium Funding helps us to further develop these valuable skills and personal attributes.
The School Games Mark Award (SGM) is a government led initiative and is delivered through the School Games Programme. At Greenmount we currently host one of the islands two School Games Organisers (SGO). The School Games Framework works to a set of values to promote lifelong participation in sport and physical activity. The School Games Values are, Honesty, Passion, Self- Belief, Teamwork, Determination and Respect. These values are promoted in every PE lesson and sports activity held at the school. Launched in 2012 the SGM rewards schools for their commitment to delivering high quality PE and the development of competition opportunities, physical activity and personal challenge across their school and into the community. Participating in the process allows schools to evaluate their PE, school sport amd Physical activity (PESSPA) provision and assists them to develop an action plan for future progress. The Platinum Award was added to the range of criteria as an extension of the SGM to reward schools who had consistently achieved 5 successive Gold level awards. Schools must first achieve the Gold award and are then are invited to submit a detailed case study with supporting evidence accompanied by a supporting statement from their School Games Organiser to achieve Platinum. Greenmount was the first island school to be awarded this prestigious Platinum SGM.
As a school we also pride ourselves on our after school sports club provision and clubs are often oversubscribed. There is a sports club held on every night of the week for KS2 pupils to attend, including a Change 4 life club. Our clubs change every half term (click here to see the current club selection) Children are encouraged to re-apply every half term to attend a sports club so that very child has the opportunity to attend at least one club per half-term. The school employs specialist sports coaches to deliver some clubs and support the PE curriculum. This includes Chelsea FC (IW) Ryde Lawns Tennis Cub, Island Table Tennis Club, IW Country Cricket Board and Shift it Cycling Instructors. We also encourage our own staff to deliver clubs. There is a well-stocked PE store and regular CPD opportunities and support for staff. The school is an active school and has an active playground scheme at lunchtimes with our MSAs supported with CPD and resources. We promote active classrooms and encourage the children to be active through personal challenges and activities.
Sports Premium Funding 2024-25

SEND
The Isle of Wight Council is committed to giving all children and young people high quality education that enables them to make progress and achieve well. For children and young people aged 0 to 25 with special educational needs or a disability, additional or specialist support may be needed to enable this. To support the process of identifying the range of provision and advice that is available, the Isle of Wight Local Authority have published a local offer. For more information about the Local Offer please use the following link: https://www.iow.gov.uk/article/2074/IW-SEND-Local-Offer
Our Special Educational Needs Co-ordinator (SENCO) is
Mrs L RichardsYou can contact her by phoning the school office on 01983 562165 or via e-mail at laura.richards@greenmount.iow.sch.uk
For more information about SEND provision at Greenmount, please see the links below:
If you have a child with special educational needs or disability you can also get advice from SENDIASS Isle of Wight. SENDIASS (IOW) offers free, impartial and confidential information, advice and support to parents, and carers of children and young people aged 0-25 with SEND as well as the young people themselves.

Curriculum Maps
For information on how the curriculum is made accessible for those with disabilities and special educational needs, please see our SEND page.
To find out more about the curriculum our school is following, please contact us on 01983 562165 or by email at contactus@greenmount.iow.sch.uk.

Headteacher’s Welcome
Hello and welcome to Greenmount Primary School.
I’m so proud to lead a school filled with happy, enthusiastic learners and a team of staff who go above and beyond every day. Our aim is simple — to make sure every child feels valued, supported, and inspired to do their best. Children are truly at the heart of everything we do.
We are a vibrant school for children aged 2 to 11 years, with our nursery incorporated into the main school to ensure smooth transitions and continuity of care as children move through each stage of their learning. From their very first days in nursery to their final year with us, every child is known, nurtured, and encouraged to flourish.
Located just a short distance from the busy town centre and beautiful local beach, our school is nestled within a residential area, close to where many of our children live. This gives us a wonderful sense of community — we’re proud to be a school right at the heart of our neighbourhood.
We’re also proud to have an on-site resourced provision which supports children with a primary need of Autism. Spaces within this provision are allocated by the Local Authority, and it plays an important role in helping us create an inclusive and understanding environment where every child can thrive.
We believe that learning should be exciting, challenging, and fun. Whether it’s in the classroom, outdoors, on the sports field, or during one of our many enrichment activities, our children are encouraged to explore their talents, build confidence, and develop a lifelong love of learning.
Thank you for visiting our website. I hope it gives you a sense of the warmth, ambition, and community spirit that make Greenmount such a special place to learn and grow.
With best wishes,Mrs Rebecca DayHeadteacher

Governing Body
On 1st October 2024, following a consultation process with parents, staff, the local community and with the support of the Isle of Wight Council, Greenmount Primary School and Gatten & Lake Primary School became The Federation of Greenmount and Gatten & Lake Primary Schools. The federation works together under a single Governing Body with one Head Teacher.
We strive to ensure that the unique character and strength of each school is recognised and celebrated. It is important to us that every child we educate identifies with the special qualities of their school and is proud to be a part of it.
Collaboration is at the very heart of the federation, with the schools working closely together to develop the very best environment to provide a first class education and wider opportunities for our children.
The Federation Governing Body is a highly effective, committed group of people who offer support and challenge as part of the effective leadership of both schools. Their role is to oversee the way that the schools are run, ensuring that they fulfil all statutory responsibilities and that the children get the best education possible.
The key functions of the Governing Body are to:
In order to meet the core functions identified above, governors undertake extensive monitoring throughout each school year. Governors assume responsibilities for clearly identified aspects of school oversight, including education performance/attainment (through data analysis), composition and effectiveness of the school curriculum, SEND, health and safety and financial management. This monitoring manifests itself in a variety of ways, including, but not limited to:
The Executive Headteacher is responsible for the internal organisation, management and control of the school and working to the objectives agreed by the governing board. The Governing Body provides the framework within which she and her staff work.
Follow the links below for further information on the Federation Governing Body:
If you have any concerns about the school these should always be raised in the first place with the Head teacher, Mrs Day who is responsible for the day to day running of the school. If you are not satisfied with the result of this or have other matters which you think should be raised with Governors you can contact them at alison.lockey_clerk@gmgl-federation.co.uk. The Chair of Governors will be happy to discuss any issues you have – but again note that day-to-day issues should be raised first with the school.
The role of the school governor is demanding but very rewarding and is a good way to give something back to your local community. If you are interested in finding out more about governance or feel you have something to offer please get in touch – again via the school office.
Further information about School Governors can be found on the Isle of Wight council website:
https://www.iow.gov.uk/article/2352/School-governor-information
